focus: A21 Pi fast-mode claim in a trusted project: zero --fast in trusted main checkout
answeredQuestions: Why does a plain `pi --help` in the trusted main checkout register no `--fast`, and what claim design registers exactly one copy in every layout?

label: Root cause confirmed (hypothesis + refinement): the pre-trust pass's claim listener survives on the shared per-loader event bus into the trusted pass, so every final-pass fast-mode copy stands down; the copy that wins the claim is the user-scope symlink alias (~/.pi/agent/extensions/pi-fast-mode-w-subagent-support -> main checkout) loaded during the untrusted pre-trust pass. Real-run instrumentation shows exactly one claim subscription (pass A) and one pass-B probe emitted into 1 listener and marked claimed.

Zero-flag mechanism: in the trusted main checkout the claimed alias entry is pruned from the final extension set by realpath dedupe (project rank 0 outranks user rank 2, canonicalizePath=realpathSync collapses alias into project copy), so --help renders zero --fast; in a worktree the alias realpath differs from the worktree copy, both entries survive, and the pass-A alias entry keeps flags=[fast] -> exactly one. -a/-na run a single pass with no pre-trust listener, so the project copy claims and registers.

Blast radius: in the trusted main checkout the stand-down early-return kills the entire extension (no /fast command, status handling or session-start wiring), not just the --fast flag; flag absence directly observed, command/handler loss inferred from the same early return at src/index.ts:123-124.

The extension source comment's conflict model (Pi fails the whole load when two copies register one flag) is contradicted by resource-loader.js:583-585: conflicts are reported as diagnostics and precedence is handled by load order.

Claim design that registers exactly one copy in every layout: register the flag before/outside the claimPackage early-return (claim keeps gating commands/handlers). Mechanically verified against all four observed layouts: main trusted -> dedupe leaves only the project copy (1 flag, no conflict); worktree trusted -> both register, load-order precedence makes the project/worktree copy effective (1 flag + diagnostic); untrusted -> alias only (1); -a/-na -> single pass (1). Residual: /fast stays dead in trusted main until the deeper fix.

Upstream fix path: release pre-trust event-bus subscriptions when reload() discards the pre-trust set, or prefer final-pass copies over pruned-path preloads in loadFinalExtensionSet. Runtime-scoping will not fix it: the final pass reuses the pre-trust runtime (resource-loader.js:560,577) and invalidate() only fires on session replacement.

Ruled out empirically: release-on-project_trust claim design (sandbox: reload() re-runs the pre-trust pass internally, re-claim re-pruned); realpath-keyed claim with same-file takeover (fragile across a second reload on the same loader, no eviction primitive). Also recorded: calling loadProjectTrustExtensions() before reload({resolveProjectTrust}) double-runs the pre-trust pass and distorts which copy claims (harness artifact, not a Pi bug).

Observed ground truth: pi --offline --help --fast counts = main plain 0, main -a 1, main -na 1, worktree plain 1, worktree -a 1, worktree -na 1; user-level fast-mode copy is a symlink to the main checkout copy; extension sources identical across trees; pi 1.3.0 dist matches the read files.

direction: Release the claim listener on the project_trust event
reason: Sandbox-refuted: reload({resolveProjectTrust}) internally re-runs the untrusted pre-trust pass; the re-claiming alias entry is pruned by realpath dedupe again, final set still flagless.

direction: Scope the claim to the extension runtime instead of the event bus
reason: Static + harness evidence: loadFinalExtensionSet passes preTrustExtensions.runtime into the final pass and returns that same runtime, so a runtime-scoped claim behaves identically to the bus claim.

direction: Treat -a/-na vs plain difference as the mechanism
reason: wt -a and wt -na both keep exactly one --fast; the override only removes the pre-trust pass, which explains but does not differentiate the layouts.
